checks.check: The log of the run that stopped (previous=true): the last lines before the exit
The last termination reason, the exit code and when the restarts began
A rollout, ConfigMap or Secret change just before the first restart
Liveness probe failures and back-off in the pod's events
A dependency it calls at start that refuses or times out (the error line names it)
The last termination reason (OOMKilled, exit code 137) and the container's memory request and limit
Memory in use against the limit before each kill: a steady climb or a jump
Workers or threads the process starts (args, env) against the limit, and a rollout that changed either
Other pods on the same node and the node's memory: the node may have run short, not the container
Fewer ready replicas after each kill, so the rest take more load and are killed in turn
The pull error as the events write it: not found, unauthorized or a timeout
The image and tag of the failing pods against the previous revision's
The imagePullSecrets of the pod or its ServiceAccount, by name, and whether they exist in the namespace
Whether pods on other nodes pull the same image: one node's network or the registry for all
The ConfigMaps and Secrets the pods use, and when each was last written
Whether only the pods started after that write fail, while older pods keep working
The error line that names the setting or key
The Argo CD application's last sync and its revision

title: Rollout not progressing or a new revision failing

checks.check: The revisions: which image and template the new one brought and when it started
New pods against old: whether only the new revision's pods fail or stay unready
The new pods' log and their readiness probe failures
The Argo CD application or Helm release that made the revision
The NetworkPolicies that select the source and the destination pods
Whether the policies allow that source, destination and port
Dropped flows between the two in the window
When the policy was created or last written, against when the errors began
The name exactly as the error writes it: a short name read from another namespace, or a name that changed
The pod's dnsPolicy and dnsConfig
The Service that name points to: in which namespace, and whether it has ready endpoints
CoreDNS answers by response code and its errors over the window

title: CPU or memory held by its limit

checks.check: The container's CPU and memory requests and limits
The throttled share of CPU periods and the use against the limit over the window
Latency in the same window: a throttled process slows down without writing errors
A rollout that lowered a limit, or more load from fewer replicas
A LimitRange that sets the default limit
Each ResourceQuota of the namespace: used against hard
FailedCreate events of ReplicaSets, StatefulSets or Jobs that name the quota
What used it up and when: new workloads, more replicas or larger requests
The symptom further on: workloads short of replicas, so the pods left carry the load

title: Node not ready, under pressure or out of capacity

checks.check: The node's conditions and when each last changed
Whether the affected pods share that node
The node's CPU, memory and disk
Evictions and scheduling failures (insufficient CPU or memory, taints) in the events
Whether the node is new or being replaced (its creation time, the autoscaler's events)

title: A service it depends on is down

checks.check: The address the error names, the Service behind it and its ready endpoints
The dependency's own pods: status, restarts and their log at that time
Which callers fail and since when: several failing together point to what they all call, not to each caller
Other alerts firing at the same time, often from the same cause

title: A service it depends on is slow

checks.check: Where a slow request spends its time: the span that took it
The dependency's latency and request count over the window against the window before
Queues, connection pools or consumers falling behind without errors
CPU throttling or a busy node under the dependency
The PVC's phase and StorageClass and the volume's events (FailedMount, FailedAttachVolume, ProvisioningFailed)
Volume use against capacity and the days until full
Whether the volume is still attached to another node or pod
The write error in the log (no space left, read-only file system)
